In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah al-'Asr

It is Meccan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the ad-dahr (the lifetime, the passage of time), and in it is a lesson in the passing of night and day, that they follow one and the same order.

It is related from al-Hasan and Qatadah that it is al-'ashi (the late afternoon and evening).

The poet said:

(We set out with you in the morning, and the time of 'asr has been shortened, and in the first morning journey is the reward and the recompense.)

Al-'asran are the night and the day. It is also said: they are the morning (al-ghadah) and the evening (al-'ashi).

Muqatil said: al-'Asr is the prayer of 'Asr (the afternoon prayer).

It is related from some of them that it is the time (al-'asr) of the Prophet, and that He swore by it. It is also reported that in the reading of 'Ali it is: "By the time and the calamities of time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, and advise one another to truth, and advise one another to patience." And it is in it until the end of life.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: "By the Lord of the time."

His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ means: is in deficiency (ghabn). It is also said: in evil, and it is said: in destruction. Khusran (loss) is the going away of the capital (ras al-mal), and the capital of the human being is his life and his self. So when he disbelieves, his capital has gone. Al-insan (mankind) here is the disbeliever. It is also said: it is a singular used in the sense of the plural. It is also said: it refers to a specific disbeliever, and it is said: he is Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and it is said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and it is said: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 103, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿Except those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾ means: through acts of obedience.

And His saying: ﴿and advise one another to truth﴾ al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning, with the Qur'an and following it. And it was said: with monotheism (tawhid).

And from al-Suddi: "by Allah," meaning: they advised one another by Allah. And from al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, he said: they urge one another to obey Allah.

And His saying: ﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ means patience in refraining from sins. And it was said: patience in obedience. A strange report has also come, narrated through Abu Umamah, that His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ refers to Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

And His saying: ﴿Except those who have believed﴾ refers to Abu Bakr; ﴿and done righteous deeds﴾ refers to 'Umar; ﴿and advise one another to truth﴾ refers to 'Uthman; ﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ refers to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them all.
